description.value: A between-subjects fMRI study examining the relationship between food addiction symptoms and BOLD activation during anticipated and consummatory palatable food reward in healthy adolescent females.

spans.text: Between-Subjects fMRI study.

value: we hypothesized that participants exhibiting elevated FA symptoms would show greater activation in response to food cues in the amygdala, striatum, OFC, DLPFC, thalamus, midbrain, insula, and anterior cingulate gyrus.

we hypothesized that, during consumption of a highly palatable food, the high versus low FA group would demonstrate less activation in the dorsal striatum and OFC, analogous to the reduced activation demonstrated in substance dependent participants upon receipt of a drug.

The milkshake paradigm was designed to examine activation in response to consumption and anticipated consumption of palatable food ( Figure 1 ).

description.value: Participants viewed milkshake or water images signaling delivery of chocolate milkshake or a tasteless solution, with cue and receipt events.

Presentation of a milkshake image for 2 seconds signaling impending delivery of chocolate milkshake; on unpaired trials the expected taste was not delivered, allowing anticipatory BOLD response to be modeled without actual receipt. Participants had no response demand beyond viewing the cue and following the paradigm.

Presentation of a water-like image for 2 seconds signaling impending delivery of the calorie-free tasteless solution; on unpaired trials the expected taste was not delivered. Participants had no response demand beyond viewing the cue and following the paradigm.
Delivery of 0.5 ml of chocolate milkshake over 5 seconds through an intraoral manifold; participants were instructed to swallow when shown the swallow cue.
Delivery of 0.5 ml of calorie-free tasteless solution over 5 seconds through an intraoral manifold; participants were instructed to swallow when shown the swallow cue.
